text:
sasha: heads up — after the kernel-prune landed in canary (rev: a1b2c3) we started seeing 2–3x tail latency spikes on multi-turn chat with long prefixes. Observed pattern: prefill looks fine but decode latency jumps mid-stream and requests get queue-retried.
ben: can you paste the perf numbers & node id? is this only on A100 pools or also on V100?
sasha: repro on a100-64-gpu-3 (us-west). p90 pre-prune: 120ms, post-prune p90: 340ms, p99: 1.1s. Token throughput drops ~30%. Logs show a lot of small kernel switches and frequent KV cache flushes.
maria: possible hypothesis — kernel pruning removed a previously-used fused-gemm kernel for short residuals, causing more kernel handoffs. Those extra CUDA launches could be flushing the KV reuse window. Did we change our KV priming or cache eviction thresholds?
sasha: no config changes to KV thresholds in the canary. I attached a short profiler snapshot:
```
# nvprof-like output (summary)
GPU 0: launch_count 1243 -> 3121 (post)
avg_kernel_time 0.42ms -> 0.26ms (more small kernels)
KV cache DRAM hits drop 7% -> 2% (counts)
stall_time due to kernel-switch 18ms -> 78ms
```
ben: ugh. more tiny kernels means worse batching packing. Could be our batch formation heuristic now underestimates stage cost and splits batches more aggressively, leading to many prefill/decode interleaves.
ciara: I ran the loopprof on the same workload and saw a shift: stage boundary moved earlier -> decode kernels invoked with unprimed KV. Flame snippet: `prefill_conv -> prefill_attn -> decode_attn (cold_kv) -> small_reduce` repeated. Link: https://profiler.internal/reports/3329876543 (internal)
maria: quick mitigation: we can increase token_budget_target for prefill by +25% on canary to encourage larger prefill groups and reduce handshake frequency. That should increase prefill batching and keep decode paths warmer. Thoughts?
sasha: willing to try. Patch suggestion: set `phase_token_targets = {prefill: 1.25, decode: 0.9}` for canary and enable `kv_priming: aggressive` flag.
ben: add a fallback config: if kernel_switch_rate > 2.5 per-request then force `prefill_only_batching = true` for that node. That could avoid the split-phase thrash while we root cause.
ciara: also worth adding a quick metric: `kv_hit_rate_by_stage` so we can see prefill vs decode hits. Right now we only have combined kv_hit_rate which masks the problem.
sasha: agreed. I'll open a canary rollout:
```
# canary patch
curl -X POST https://deploy.internal/canary-config -d '{"nodes":["a100-64-gpu-3"], "overrides":{"phase_token_targets":{"prefill":1.25,"decode":0.9}, "kv_priming":"aggressive","prefill_only_on_high_switch":true}}'
```
runtime-bot: deploy started for canary-config (id: canary-2026-03-18-001). Rolling to 1 node.
sasha: rolling now, will monitor p50/p90/p99 + kv_hit_rate_by_stage. If we still see >1s p99 after 15m we roll back.
maria: one more note — we should check kernel selection heuristics for sequence-length buckets. Kernel prune probably merged some buckets; we might need a small exception table for mid-lengths (256-512) where fused kernels gave best latency. I'll file a follow-up issue.
ben: thanks. If the canary helps we can stage to the rest of cluster with the fallback enabled. Also let's capture a couple of decoded traces for replay in local perf harness.
ciara: adding the kv_hit_rate_by_stage metric now (prometheus exporter patch). ETA ~25m.
sasha: update (3329876575): initial canary metrics — p90 down to 180ms, p99 down to 420ms, kv_hit_rate_by_stage: prefill 8%->18%, decode 3%->5%. Not back to baseline but big improvement. Continuing watch.
ben: nice. keep an eye on cost (more prefill batching increases GPU occupancy). If cost regresses too much we may iterate on kernel selection to restore small-kernel efficiency.
sasha: will follow up with a short postmortem if this ends up being a regression. For now the canary stabilizes.
ciara: prometheus exporter in: https://git.internal/r/prod/exp/3329876543 — grafana panels updated.
sasha: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
